Classical calendar variation model

Source: R/classic.R
calvar_classic.Rd

Regression with ARIMA errors in which a moving holiday enters as a dummy for the period that contains it and has the same effect in every year: Yt=β0+β1t+St+αVt+Nt,Y_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 t + S_t + \alpha V_t + N_t,Yt​=β0​+β1​t+St​+αVt​+Nt​, where Vt=1V_t = 1Vt​=1 if period ttt contains the holiday, StS_tSt​ is the seasonal component and NtN_tNt​ an ARIMA process. This is the calendar variation model commonly used in applied work and the benchmark for [lunarcast()], which contains it as a special case.

Usage

calvar_classic(
  y,
  dates,
  trend = c("deterministic", "stochastic"),
  season = c("dummy", "fourier", "stochastic"),
  K = frequency(y)/2 - 1,
  lambda = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

y

Monthly or quarterly `ts`.

dates

`Date` vector of holiday occurrences.

trend

`"deterministic"` or `"stochastic"`.

season

`"dummy"`, `"fourier"` or `"stochastic"`.

K

Number of Fourier pairs for `season = "fourier"` (default 5 for monthly data).

lambda

Box-Cox parameter; `NULL` (default) keeps the original scale, so the holiday effect is additive.

...

Passed to [forecast::auto.arima()].

Value

An object of class `"calvar_classic"`.

Details

The six structures of the classical approach combine a trend and a seasonal component:

modeltrendseasonality
m1deterministicdummy
m2deterministicFourier
m3stochasticdummy
m4stochasticFourier
m5deterministicstochastic (seasonal ARIMA)
m6stochasticstochastic (seasonal ARIMA)

"Deterministic" adds the linear trend regressor β1t\beta_1 tβ1​t; "stochastic" leaves the trend to differencing. In both cases the ARIMA orders, including the order of differencing, are chosen by [forecast::auto.arima()]. Seasonal dummies use the last season (December) as reference.

See also

[calvar_classic_all()] for the six structures at once and [lunarcast()] for the proposed model.

Examples

m1 <- calvar_classic(sapi, holiday_dates("idul_adha"),
                     trend = "deterministic", season = "dummy")
m1
#> Classical calendar variation model: deterministic trend + dummy seasonality 
#> Regression with ARIMA(3,0,1) errors | AICc = 1851.4 
#> Holiday effect (same every year): 29.78 (s.e. 1.72), original scale
forecast(m1, h = 12)
